agent_notes: This working-tree diff exactly undoes the template half of HEAD commit 542d5dd. That commit's message names the bug this diff brings back. The orchestrator confirmed the regression test fails.

A single <form> cannot wrap both the General fields and the instance fields, because the Security <form> (save_security, line 97) sits between them and HTML does not allow nested forms. The comment deleted by this diff said exactly this. Associating fields with a form via form="id" is the established way this template handles that limit (add-instance forms, lines 228-232 and 250).

The bug is worse than the General fields simply not saving. routes.py:531-539 fills in hard-coded defaults rather than keeping current_settings.general values when a key is missing. So any POST without the General keys overwrites the user's existing values. Only tracking_delay_seconds (line 537) keeps the current value. A separate hardening step would be to fall back to current_settings.general for missing keys, the same way instances are kept when no instance keys are present. That change is outside this diff and belongs to the bugs/correctness lane.
No import cycles, new dependencies, or cross-module reach-ins: the change only touches a Jinja template. save_settings and save_security in routes.py are unchanged.

Stale-comment risk: the diff deletes the explanatory comments (lines 18-21 and 137-139 in HEAD) that stopped this exact mistake from happening. If 542d5dd is restored, those comments come back with it.

agent_notes: Blast radius: one template (triggarr/templates/settings.html) and one handler (save_settings at triggarr/web/routes.py:520). No Python API signatures, schema or migrations change. The data impact still reaches the persisted config.toml and the live scheduler, because routes.py:529-540 rebuilds the whole [general] block from form.get() with safe_int/safe_log_level defaults and never falls back to current_settings, except tracking_delay_seconds.

What goes wrong: every press of the only 'Save Settings' button (settings.html:243) writes [general] = {log_level='info', hard_max_per_cycle=0, max_history_rows=1000, request_timeout=30, page_size=50, tracking_window_minutes=60, max_consecutive_failures=5, skip_unreleased=false}. Pydantic validation passes because these are valid defaults, so no warning is logged and the user gets a normal 303 redirect.

Behavioral consequences after a reset: skip_unreleased silently turns off, so the daemon starts searching unreleased titles. request_timeout and page_size revert, which changes outbound *arr load. max_history_rows reverts to 1000, so history pruning may delete rows beyond that cap. That deletion can't be undone.

The instances side is unaffected. The instances form still posts {app}__{instance}__{field} keys and keeps API keys when the field is left empty. The Security form (line 97, save_security) is unaffected.

This diff is a byte-exact reversal of the template half of HEAD commit 542d5dd, which was explicitly a walkthrough fix for this bug. The old comment explaining why form="settings-form" is required (nested forms are illegal because the Security form sits between the two sections) was deleted, and that constraint still holds.
Verdict: Blocking. This reintroduces a silent config-overwrite regression and fails the existing regression test. Discard the working-tree change.
